blocks.text: If you're running your first TCS Sydney Marathon, here's the short version: it's on Sunday 30 August 2026, starts on the North Sydney side of the Harbour Bridge and crosses it before finishing on the Opera House forecourt, and it's now one of the Abbott World Marathon Majors — the same club as Boston, London and New York. I live and write here in Bondi, so this is the beginner's guide I wish someone had handed me.
The course, and why it's tougher than it looks

It's a point-to-point course over the Harbour Bridge on closed roads, through The Rocks and Barangaroo, out to the eastern parklands around Moore Park and Centennial Park, then back to that unforgettable finish beside the Opera House. Don't let the harbour views fool you — there are some genuine hills through the middle, so pull up the official elevation profile, bank patience early, and save your legs for them.

blocks.title: Bondi isn't on the route
blocks.text: A lot of visitors assume the marathon sweeps past Bondi Beach — it doesn't. The course stays closer to the harbour and the inner-eastern parklands. Bondi still makes a brilliant base for the weekend, and a great place to recover once you've got the medal.

The headline event is the full marathon (42.195 km) on the Sunday. There's also a family-friendly 5 km Mini Marathon, held on the Saturday of race weekend. Worth flagging so you're not caught out: the 10 km event is not part of the 2026 program, so double-check the current line-up on the official site before you build your weekend around it.

items: Mini Marathon (5 km) — Saturday 29 August 2026, great for kids and first-timers
Entry is by ballot/lottery — check the official site for charity or tour places

blocks.text: Getting there, road closures and your bib

Race morning is not a drive-and-park situation. Expect major road closures across the Harbour Bridge, the CBD and the eastern route, so treat public transport as plan A. I won't quote exact train lines or start-group access — the organisers fine-tune it each year, so check the official travel information and Transport for NSW close to the day and work from the current map.

blocks.title: You must collect your own bib
blocks.text: Bibs are collected in person at the event expo ("The Running Show") in the days before the race — bring photo ID, as friends or family generally can't pick up for you. Confirm the current expo dates, venue and opening hours on the official site first.

Base yourself in Bondi and use the buses and ferries to get back east after you finish. My legs thank me more for a slow amble along the promenade and a flat white than for collapsing onto a hotel bed.

You don't need to overthink your first marathon. Build your long runs gradually over a few months, get comfortable on hills so the mid-course rollers don't surprise you, and practise your fuelling — never try a new gel, breakfast or pair of shoes on the start line. Bring a throwaway layer for the cool morning, start slower than feels natural, and let the Opera House pull you home.

stops.title: Collect your bib
stops.detail: The Running Show with photo ID — check dates and venue on the official site.

stops.title: Mini Marathon & shakeout
stops.detail: Cheer the Mini, do a gentle jog, lay out your kit, sleep early.

stops.title: Public transport to the North Sydney start
stops.detail: No driving. Follow the official travel plan, throwaway warm layer on.

stops.title: Opera House & recovery
stops.detail: Refuel, then head east to Bondi for a promenade walk and a coffee.

items.q: When is the 2026 TCS Sydney Marathon?
items.a: The full marathon is on Sunday 30 August 2026, with the 5 km Mini Marathon on Saturday 29 August 2026. Confirm start-wave timings on the official website, as they're finalised closer to the day.

items.q: Where does the marathon start and finish?
items.a: It starts on the North Sydney side of the Sydney Harbour Bridge, crosses the bridge, and finishes on the forecourt of the Sydney Opera House. It does not run through Bondi Beach.

items.q: How do I enter the Sydney Marathon?
items.a: Now that Sydney is an Abbott World Marathon Major, general entry is run as a ballot (lottery). Check the official site for the current entry window, plus any charity or travel-package places.

items.q: Can I still run the 10 km?
items.a: The 10 km event is not part of the 2026 program. The 5 km Mini Marathon is the shorter option that weekend — verify the current line-up on the official site.

items.q: Is Bondi a good base for the marathon?
items.a: It's a lovely weekend base and a great place to recover, but the course doesn't come to Bondi — you'll need public transport to the north-side start on race morning.

blocks.text: Whether you're chasing a Major star or just want to say you ran across the Harbour Bridge with no cars in sight, your first Sydney Marathon is special. Do the boring things well — sleep, fuel, logistics — and let race day be the fun part. Afterwards, come find us in Bondi — the ocean's the best ice bath in town.
